papers.title_en: FOCUS & RePAIR: Mitigating Text Degeneration via Token-Level Guidance for Pruned Large Language Models
papers.authors: Junyoung Lee, Sehyeon Park, Shinhyoung Jang, Seonha Ryu, Hojeong Kim, Hyunsei Lee, Il Hong Suh, Yeseong Kim
papers.evidence: 剪枝后LLM的token级引导微调，围绕压缩与适配主题
papers.tldr: 针对大语言模型剪枝后出现的文本退化（尤其重复循环）问题，本文从token级视角将解码视为动态过程，将退化拆解为循环进入风险与循环持久性。基于此提出FOCUS与RePAIR两种token级指导目标：FOCUS重加权蒸馏以抑制高置信泄漏，RePAIR通过以起始为中心的正负续写对与边际损失促进合理替代，防止过早陷入重复。实验表明两种方法均有效降低重复并提升生成质量，为剪枝后微调提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Pruning is a practical approach to compress large language models (LLMs), but it can amplify text degeneration, especially repetition loops, even when perplexity and task accuracy remain largely unchanged. In this work, we present a token-level analysis of this failure mode by viewing decoding as a dynamical process that enters and persists in a small set of recurrent contexts. Our analysis decomposes degeneration into loop entry risk and loop persistence, and shows that persistence is controlled by the escape mass assigned to plausible alternatives within the token sampling set. Motivated by these findings, we propose two token-level guidance objectives for post-pruning fine-tuning. FOCUS reweights distillation toward high-confidence teacher regions to suppress leakage, while RePAIR uses onset-centered positive/negative continuation pairs with a margin loss to promote plausible alternatives and prevent early commitment to repetition loops. Experiments on open-ended continuation and instruction-based generation show that both methods consistently reduce repetition and improve generation quality.
